{{Short description|German mathematician (born 1954)}}
'''Albrecht Böttcher''' (born 29 December 1954) is a German mathematician. His field of research is [[functional analysis]].

==History==
Böttcher was born in [[Oberwiesenthal]], Saxony, [[GDR]]. Between 1971 and 1973, he was in an elite class for mathematics at the [[Chemnitz University of Technology]]. In 1973, he won a silver medal at the 15th [[International Math Olympiad]] in Moscow.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://imo-official.org/participant_r.aspx?id=10265 |title=International Mathematical Olympiad |first= |last= |work=imo-official.org |year=2011 |access-date=7 April 2011 |archive-date=18 August 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110818113139/http://imo-official.org/participant_r.aspx?id=10265 }}</ref> Böttcher studied mathematics from 1975 to 1979 in [[Chemnitz]] and then went to [[Rostov on Don]] in 1980 to study and earned a PhD there in 1984. After completing his dissertation, ''The finite section method for the Wiener-Hopf integral operator,''<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=29340}}</ref> he worked as scientist assistance at the university of Chemnitz. Since 1992, the professor for ''Harmonic Analysis and Operator theory'' at the Chemnitz University of Technology. Since 2020 he is professor emeritus.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Pressestelle|title=Sie setzten Akzente in der Mathematik, Elektro- und Informationstechnik sowie in der Physikalischen Chemie|url=https://www.tu-chemnitz.de/tu/pressestelle/aktuell/10357|access-date=30 November 2020|website=www.tu-chemnitz.de|language=de}}</ref>

{{As of|2012}}, he is the author of nine books and about 180 papers.<ref>{{Cite web
 |url= http://www-user.tu-chemnitz.de/~aboettch/vita.html
 |title=Albrecht Böttcher
 |work=www-user.tu-chemnitz.de
 |access-date=15 October 2010
}}</ref>
